feature: A Forever spinner goes round at its own pace
summary: A spinner set to Forever now turns every Over milliseconds whatever the loop's length, so an 800 ms spinner beside a 900 ms bell no longer stops for a tenth of a second each turn, on the canvas or in the exported SVG. The strip draws its next turn as a dashed bar after the real one.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Draw a rectangle, pick it, and choose Rotation from the plus on Motion (the 900 ms bell swing).
Draw an ellipse, pick it, and add Rotation to it too.
On the ellipse's Rotation set From 0, To 360, Curve Linear, Repeat Forever, Over 800.
Look at the strip: the ellipse's bar ends at 800 ms and a dashed copy carries on past the repeats line.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press play and watch the ellipse: it turns steadily, with no catch where the bell's loop starts over.
Copy or export the SVG and open it in a browser: the spinner turns without a hitch while the bell swings.

evaluate: Does the spinner now turn without any catch while the bell swings beside it?
Does the dashed bar after the spinner read as "it goes round again" rather than as a second motion?
Is Forever meaning "every Over milliseconds" what you expect, now that a Forever motion longer than the loop also keeps going rather than being cut off?
rough: The mock's strip says "800 ms per turn" and "ends where it starts" for a spinner; the app's strip still says only the whole loop length ("900 ms follows the longest"). Filed as the-timing-strip-says-how-long-one-turn-of-a-for.

Only one way Forever keeps its own pace. Forever, there and back still shares the loop, so a 600 ms there-and-back beside a 900 ms bell rests at home for 300 ms each loop. That is a rest at home rather than a stutter, and it is what keeps two swings in step.
A Forever motion on a video clip now repeats every Over too, where before it played once per clip. New motions on a clip arrive as Once, so this only changes a motion someone set to Forever by hand.
The Forever motion still counts toward the loop's length, so a 1200 ms spinner beside a 900 ms bell stretches the loop to 1200 and the bell rests 300 ms each loop. Left in the task log.
